proxy_language: Proto-Vedda substrate as reflected in Sinhala Vedda (Vedda/Wanniyala-Aetto) lexical remnants, with Proto-Sinhalese/Elu Prakrit as the structural scaffold
proxy_rationale: Balangoda culture (Pleistocene-Holocene, c. 38,000-3,000 BP, Sri Lanka; Balangoda Man, Fa Hien Lena, Batadomba-lena) has no linguistic record. The only living-language window is the Vedda (Wanniyala-Aetto) speech variety, which was largely absorbed into Sinhala, and the pre-Sinhala lexical substrate studied by Geiger, Wijesekera and Deraniyagala. Vedda remnants show Indo-Aryan structure with an unexplained non-Indo-Aryan lexical residue. Any link to the Balangoda people is hypothetical, as continuity is argued from skeletal and genetic data only. Names should therefore sound Sinhala-Vedda-like, with simple open syllables, and should not be presented as attested Balangoda speech.
phonology: Vowels: a, i, u, e, o, each short or long (a, ae, i, u, e, o; long vowels marked with macron in scholarly transliteration, plain Latin for gameplay). Consonants (Sinhala/Vedda-like): stops p b t d k g with a dental/retroflex contrast, affricates c j (spelled ch, j), nasals m n ng, liquids l r, fricatives s h, glides v y. Prenasalized stops (mb nd ng) occur in Sinhala and are typical of the Vedda-adjacent lexicon. Vowel length is contrastive; no tone. Stress falls on the first syllable.
phonotactics: Dominant shape (C)V(C), with open syllables favoured (CV, CVCV, CVCVCV). Initial consonant clusters are absent in native words. Word-internal clusters are limited to geminates (kk, tt, dd, pp, mm, nn, ll) and nasal + homorganic stop (mb, nd, ng, nj). Words end in a vowel, or occasionally n, m, or a geminate-final form in loanwords. No word-initial ng except in the Vedda-flavoured onomatopoeic roots. No f, z, x, w, q in native words.
orthography: Latin transliteration in the Sinhala romanization tradition: ch for the affricate, j, sh avoided in favour of s, ng for the velar nasal, ae for the open front vowel; long vowels doubled (aa, ii, uu) for gameplay in place of macrons; no diacritics required.
morphology: Agglutinative-suffixing, based on Sinhala. Nouns are inflected by suffix for case (nominative-oblique stem, genitive -ge, locative -e/-ta, instrumental -in/-en). Plurals are formed with -o/-vaa or reduplication. Definiteness and animacy follow Sinhala, where animate and inanimate nouns have distinct case patterns. Verb roots end in -a/-e and are followed by tense suffixes. Vedda-flavoured vocabulary favours short two-syllable roots (CVCV) such as terms for the forest, animals and tools, with reduplication for intensity or plurality (e.g. gala-gala).
compounding: Right-headed compounds: modifier + head (Sinhala gal-leNa = stone cave). Genitive constructions place the possessor first, linked by -ge or by simple juxtaposition: possessor-ge + head ('X of Y' = Y-ge X). Agent nouns use verbal stems plus -aa/-ekaa or the compounds karu-vaa; 'Y-maker' is built as object + karaNa(-aa) or object + kaara. Adjectives precede nouns and take no agreement.
noun_phrase_order: Modifier-head: demonstrative, adjective or genitive precedes the head noun; numerals precede the noun. Relative clauses precede the head.

attested_roots.gloss: mouth; also cave in some dialect reports
cave, rockshelter (Sinhala lena, as in Fa Hien Lena)
hill, high ground (Sinhala, as in Balangoda)
branch of a tree, in some Sinhala dialects

notes: No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word. Treat all output as speculative flavour: the link between Balangoda Pleistocene foragers and later Vedda speech is unproven, and the proxy rests on Sinhala phonology and morphology with the Vedda substrate as a stylistic overlay. Existing game names such as Ngogisu chihutsi use clusters and endings (-tsi, initial ng, final ch spellings) that are not Sinhala-like and should be replaced with CV(C)-based forms such as Galalena or Kele-ge.
